thread_analysis.thread_summary: Internal Allion thread (forwarded from Denso Ten customer). Customer asks how long registration takes after the final PTS profile test passes, and when required documents must be submitted given a December 20 registration deadline. Sakai explains that registration work is prepared in parallel with testing so that registration can be completed the business day after the last profile passes. Required documents: (1) SIG Invoice by mid-November; (2) Registration Proxy Confirmation Form by December 13.
all_questions_found: If all profile tests pass in the next session, when can SIG registration be completed?
When must required documents (Invoice, Registration Proxy Confirmation Form) be submitted?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Allion's registration process runs in parallel with PTS testing. By the time testing completes, the registration is already prepared and staged. Registration can typically be completed the business day after the last profile test passes. The critical document for timing is the SIG Invoice: it must be submitted early enough to allow the SIG payment processing time (~3 weeks from Invoice submission to SIG confirming receipt and issuing the RN). Invoice late submission = registration date slip regardless of when testing finishes.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: The critical path in the registration timeline is SIG payment processing (~3 weeks), not the registration portal submission (1–3 days). The Invoice must be submitted well before the target registration date. Parallel registration prep removes registration work from the critical path post-testing.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer submits the Invoice late, SIG's ~3-week payment processing period will push the RN issuance (and therefore registration completion) past the contract deadline. Registration work cannot compensate for late Invoice submission.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Sakai noted (honestly) that predicting PTS test pass rates for a product with many failing items is difficult. The assumption of 'all tests pass in the next session' is optimistic. The more pressing risk here is the Invoice deadline — if testing continues past mid-November, the Invoice cannot be obtained on time for a December 20 registration.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For fixed-deadline registration projects, the Invoice submission deadline is the true deadline driver — not the test completion date. Always communicate the Invoice deadline to customers early and explain the ~3-week SIG payment processing period.
